title: Colony and Horizon Anew
premise: Tamsin Villalobos smuggles memories past the customs ring of Meridian Colony while quietly maintaining an orbital beacon whose original commission records have been erased. When the colony's children begin dreaming a shared dream—a countdown, a door, a voice that knows his name—he learns the beacon is a cryosleep activation key left by the colony's founders, and that Meridian's ruling families have been editing the population's inherited memories for generations to decide who gets to wake when the jump window opens. As the children's dream spreads to adults and the colony fractures into factions, Tamsin must choose which half of humanity wakes before the window closes, ultimately refusing both the founders' list and the families' counter-list by waking the children themselves—the only generation untainted by edited memory—and seeding a new colony beyond the horizon.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade on remote stations before turning to fiction, and her work is known for its quiet, salt-worn prose and its fascination with signals sent into the dark. She writes from a coastal town whose location she declines to specify, claiming the ambiguity keeps her honest.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Paid For
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He runs contraband memory-chips past customs in a gutted freight skiff, then detours to maintain a beacon with no owner on record. Establishes his invisibility as survival. Beat: lonely competence, a ritual kept out of stubbornness.

chapters.title: Customs and Contraband
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine bribe goes wrong when inspector Yara Okafor scans a chip that shouldn't exist—a memory of Meridian's founding that contradicts the official archive. Beat: first crack in his careful anonymity.

chapters.title: The Children's Dream
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her daughter wakes screaming a dream of a countdown and a door. Other children report the same. Yara files it as hysteria; the report is quietly deleted by someone above her. Beat: institutional dread.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The beacon begins transmitting a pattern he didn't program. His smuggler contact, old Ferro, warns him someone is asking questions about the beacon's commission. Beat: the past reaching for him.

chapters.title: Found Family, Small Hours
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV at Ferro's dockside kitchen, where smugglers, dockhands, and Ferro's granddaughter Nia share a meal. Introduces the found-family web that sustains the invisible. Beat: warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: The Edited Archive
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She pulls founding-era records and finds seams: names removed, a second cryoship erased from history. Her superiors notice her curiosity. Beat: the horror of inherited lies.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Dream
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. In the shared dream, the door speaks with a voice the children all recognize—and Nia realizes it's the voice from the beacon recordings Tamsin plays at the dock. Beat: innocent revelation.

chapters.title: A Buyer Named Ashgrave
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Councillor Ashgrave offers Tamsin a fortune to smuggle a sealed memory core off-station, no questions. Tamsin recognizes the core's casing: beacon manufacture. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He decrypts the beacon's buried log: it is a cryosleep activation key, and its commission was signed by the second ship's captain—the one history deleted. Beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Smuggler
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara detains Tamsin, not for smuggling but for answers. They trade truths across a table: her erased records, his beacon log. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: two loners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Astronomy confirms it: a stable jump window opens in eight months, and the beacon's key determines which cryopods wake. Whoever holds the key chooses humanity's next branch. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's List
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. He reveals the ruling families have curated the wake-list for generations—only their bloodlines and loyalists. He offers Tamsin a place on it. Beat: seductive corruption.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Adults start dreaming the countdown. Panic sermons in the plaza. The colony's quiet order begins to fray at the edges. Beat: contagion of hope and fear.

chapters.title: Ferro's Price
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ferro admits he helped hide the beacon decades ago and paid for it with his brother's disappearance. He begs Tamsin to burn it. Beat: guilt passed down like inheritance.

chapters.title: Yara's Daughter
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ashgrave's people threaten Yara through her daughter. She must choose: her career and safety, or the truth she's uncovered. Beat: a mother's reckoning.

chapters.title: The Second Ship
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the wreck-fields beyond customs, Tamsin finds the second cryoship's hull—scuttled, not lost. Thousands of pods, still powered, still dreaming. Beat: grave-site awe.

chapters.title: Pods and People
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The sleepers aboard are the founders' exiles: dissidents, the poor, the inconvenient. The dream is leaking from their pods into the colony's children. Beat: grief for the erased.

chapters.title: A Deal in the Dark
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ashgrave forces the issue: help him seize the beacon and purge the second ship, or Ferro and Nia pay the price. Beat: coercion tightening the noose.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Council
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The dockside family debates: flee, fight, or hand the key over. Nia argues the children dreamed the door open, not shut. Beat: found family choosing courage.

chapters.title: Sabotage at Customs
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara falsifies manifests to move the beacon key, burning her career in a single keystroke. Beat: the fall that feels like freedom.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Coup
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. With the window closing, Ashgrave seizes the orbital ring and declares emergency authority. The families' counter-list is loaded into the wake-system. Beat: the machinery of injustice in motion.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Pods
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin and Yara infiltrate the ring through smuggler routes. The beacon's log reveals the captain's final message: the key was meant for everyone, or no one. Beat: moral clarity forming.

chapters.title: Nia's Door
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. In the dream, Nia reaches the door and finds it isn't locked—it's waiting for a name to be spoken. The children begin speaking names: the exiles' names. Beat: innocence as resistance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Dock
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A member of the dock family sells their route to Ashgrave's enforcers. Ferro is taken; Tamsin escapes with the key and his guilt. Beat: the cost of trust.

chapters.title: The Wake-List War
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Colony-wide standoff: families vs. dockworkers vs. the dreaming children. Ashgrave broadcasts the official history; Yara counter-broadcasts the erased one. Beat: society splitting along the seam of memory.

chapters.title: What Ferro Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV under interrogation-adjacent tension, trading himself for Ferro. Ashgrave reveals the final cruelty: the beacon can only wake half the pods before the window closes. Beat: the choice made unavoidable.

chapters.title: The Half That Wakes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He weighs the lists: the families' curated few, or the exiles' thousands. Yara argues for neither. Beat: the thematic heart—justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Children's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The children present their own answer: wake no one's list, wake the children's chosen—the exiles, the young, the unedited. Beat: hope with hard edges.

chapters.title: Assault on the Ring
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The smugglers' fleet, patched and desperate, runs the blockade while Yara opens the ring's doors from inside. Beat: kinetic climax begins.

chapters.title: Ferro's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ferro, captive, broadcasts the beacon's true commission across every colony channel before Ashgrave cuts the feed. Beat: sacrifice and testimony.

chapters.title: The Key Turned
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV at the beacon itself. He enters the captain's override: the key splits the window, waking the exiles' pods and locking the families' list behind a generation-long delay. Beat: the choice, made and irreversible.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Horizon
chapters.summary: Ashgrave's POV. Denied his inheritance, Ashgrave orders the ring scuttled rather than lose it. Yara confronts him in the control spine. Beat: villainy as grief for lost entitlement.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The jump window seals with the exiles' ship free and the ring crippled. Ashgrave is arrested by his own security, abandoned by the families. Beat: catharsis without triumph.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The first exiles wake to a colony that half-remembers them. Reunions, accusations, a woman who recognizes Ferro's brother's name. Beat: tender disorientation.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The colony holds no trial but a reading: every erased name spoken aloud. Tamsin's own family history surfaces in the list—he is descended from the exiles. Beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: Nia's Beacon
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. The children, with Tamsin teaching, take over beacon maintenance as a civic duty. The dream fades as the sleepers wake. Beat: generational handoff.

chapters.title: Ashgrave's Cell
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara visits Ashgrave in custody. No vengeance—just the archive, unedited, left with him to read. Beat: justice as exposure, not punishment.

chapters.title: Provisions for the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The exiles' ship is refitted for a new jump toward an unclaimed horizon. Some stay, some go. Tamsin is asked to pilot the first supply run. Beat: bittersweet departure prep.

chapters.title: The Jump
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin jumps with the exiles' ship, Yara and Nia aboard as chosen family, leaving Ferro's dock in trusted hands. Beat: release—the invisible man finally seen, and choosing the open dark.

chapters.title: Horizon Anew
chapters.summary: Nia's POV, years later. A new colony takes root; the beacon's twin burns overhead, commissioned openly this time, signed by everyone. The children dream ordinary dreams. Beat: peace, inheritance made honest, found family as the true colony.
